articles.title: The Portuguese House review – picturesque, polite drama of secrets and revelations at a country estate
articles.summary: Spanish drama about people leaving their old lives behind plays out like a literary novel, with Manolo Solo excellent as a discombobulated gardener. Out of the blue, a woman walks out on her husband.
body: Manolo Solo gives an excellent performance as the left-behind husband, Fernando, an introspective mild-mannered geography professor. After his wife’s disappearance, Fernando goes on holiday to Portugal, where he meets a gardener called Manuel. When Manuel drops dead of a heart attack, Fernando decides – like his wife – to leave his old life behind; he assumes Manuel’s identity and takes a job as the gardener at a Portuguese country estate. The owner, Amália (Maria de Medeiros), senses that this intellectual man with glasses and a clumsy way with the loppers is not the man she hired, but doesn’t push it – possibly because she is attracted to him.

Like a doorstop paperback, The Portuguese House is an expansive watch, spanning years and going at a gentle pace for nearly two hours. There are more secrets and lies to come – and another person pretending to be someone they are not. That would be a twist too far in another film, but works here in a restrained drama that treats all its characters generously and with sympathy. Though in the end I wondered if it is possibly too respectful, sweeping away difficult hard-to-shift feelings like autumn leaves.
points: Spanish drama about people leaving their old lives behind plays out like a literary novel, with Manolo Solo excellent as a discombobulated gardener.

articles.title: Should the BBC and Channel 4 Merge? Sony Pictures Television’s International Production Boss Wayne Garvie Thinks So
articles.summary: The ongoing difficulties faced by the U.K.’s public service broadcasters could be partially alleviated by a dramatic merger between two of the four main players, the BBC and Channel 4.
body: “That’s what I would I do. I think it’ll probably happen, because frankly it’s very difficult to see how Channel Four survives in its present form. And it’s not it’s fault. It’s that the market is changing in every conceivable moment.”

A potential merger between the BBC and Channel 4, which would be a monumental shakeup in the U.K. TV industry, has been mooted before. Back in 2024, reports emerged that the idea was being discussed, a move that at the was claimed would add more than $1.3 billion to the BBC’s coffers and enable Channel 4’s to cut costs, free up budget to be spent on commissioning new programmes and use its profits to subsidise other parts of the BBC.

According to The Guardian, another reported model was for Channel 4 — which several years ago was under threat of privatisation by the then Conservative government — to operate as a semi-independent entity under BBC Studios, the BBC’s for-profit arm.
At the time, a BBC spokesperson said there were “no ongoing discussions” about the merger of the BBC and Channel 4 “nor are we developing a proposal to do so.”

body: Day pointed out that first-time filmmakers were generating concept art and short films that “bring their pitch to life” while Prime Video was using it to “transform the viewing experience” for its audiences via personalized recommendations, simplified synopses, spoiler-free summaries, audio descriptions and subtitles.
She said that Prime Video’s YA series “Maxton Hall” was now using lip sync technology to synchronize actors’ lib movements with human dubbed audio in different languages.
Most recently, we introduced lip sync technology on Maxton Hall, our most watched international original, which synchronizes actors’ lip movements with human dubbed audio.
Day added that “ethical guardrails” were required in using AI, however, saying they “cannot be an afterthought, they have to be the foundation and that’s the approach we’re taking.”

articles.title: Durban FilmMart Head on Why This Year’s Event Is ‘Looking Inward’ as African Screen Industries Strive to ‘Create Solutions’ on Their Own Terms
articles.summary: The Durban FilmMart returns for its 17th edition with a full slate of conversations and events looking to build on the legacy of innovation, disruption and industry-defining discussions at what is arguably the most influential film market on the continent. Running from Oct.
body: The four-day event features a wide range of panel discussions, masterclasses, one-on-one meetings and mentorship sessions designed to capitalize on a moment of unprecedented visibility — and unparalleled disruption — for the African screen industries.

In a departure from previous editions, which ran parallel to the Durban Intl. Film Festival, this year’s DFM will open with a screening, of Rwandan debutante Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo’s Cannes Caméra d’Or winner “Ben’Imana.” The film, an alumnus of DFM’s influential pitching and finance forum, was selected to highlight the event’s outsized impact on the African filmmaking community.

“This was a DFM project. It was pitched at DFM two years ago, and they were able to win two awards at Cannes [including the FIPRESCI prize],” says Reddy. “For us, the celebration of hosting a screening at the market — which we’ve not done previously — is based on the fact that we want to show our local content in our local context.”

A crucial pillar of every DFM is its influential Think Tank strand, whose conversations and conclusions often “become a blueprint for the next DFM and the direction which the industry is going,” according to Reddy.

articles.title: Sir Ranulph Fiennes' relatives tell BBC it's 'very painful' not being able to visit him
articles.summary: It has been alleged that Sir Ranulph has been admitted to a number of care homes under assumed names.
body: Relatives of the British explorer Sir Ranulph Fiennes have said it is "very painful" he appears to have been hidden away from them.
Speaking to BBC Newsnight, his former sister-in-law told the BBC that she did not know where he was, and nobody had been able to see him.
Louise Millington-Cotes did not immediately respond to the allegations, or the BBC's request for comment.
Cheshire Police have said they are aware of the concerns regarding Sir Ranulph, and are satisfied he is living in an appropriate setting with suitable care.

articles.title: Netflix’s ‘The Eternaut’ Effect: Subscriber Impact Estimate Disclosed at Iberseries
articles.summary: Korean demand drives Spanish- and Portuguese-language content growth, while U.S. gains suggest a "semi-saturated" market, a Parrot Analytics expert also tells Iberseries & Platino Industria in Madrid.
body: One of the surprise takeaways: South Korea has been a key driver of demand growth for Spanish- and Portuguese-language (SPLATAM) content.

The Parrot vp also told the Iberseries crowd that in 2025, for the first time, non-SPLATAM markets accounted for the majority of SPLATAM content demand worldwide. And he highlighted key markets that have experienced particularly strong SPLATAM series demand over the 2024-2026 period. Leading the charge was Korea, which registered a 243 percent gain, according to Parrot, followed by Japan, which saw 148 percent growth.
Other key growth market cited by Otero were Turkey (up 132 percent), China (119 percent), Sweden (103 percent) and Sweden (102 percent).

articles.title: I paid £30,000 for an 'influencer' degree. Here's why
articles.summary: Content creation degrees aim to help people make money from social media, but are they worth the money?
body: As university courses go it may raise a few eyebrows, but Destiny McGowan has no doubt that hers was very useful.
In July the 21-year-old graduated from Nottingham Trent University with a degree in content creation.
As well as teaching how to best make videos and posts for Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, the course also focused on how to build audiences, engage with brands and monetise your content.

"I always wanted to be an entrepreneur, so for me the course was about the transferable skills that I believed I would gain," says Destiny, pointing to both the social media and business aspects she was taught.
